local.h: Cancellations mount as Isaias nears Georgia
local.b: Metro Atlanta events are being canceled as Hurricane Isaias approaches Georgia.
local.title: Metro Atlanta cancellations mount as Hurricane Isaias approaches Georgia

local.h: Waffle House Index gauges storm severity
local.b: If a Waffle House stays open in a storm, Southerners and FEMA take it as a sign of how severe conditions are.
local.title: Waffle House Index helps Southerners gauge a storm's severity

local.h: Turner family asks Jackson to drop ads
local.b: The family of Secoriea Turner, 8, killed in Atlanta in 2020, urged GOP governor candidate Rick Jackson to stop using her name and image in campaign ads.
local.title: Secoriea Turner's family urges Jackson to stop using her in ads

local.h: Kemp declares state of emergency for Isaias
local.b: Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp declared a state of emergency across all 159 counties as Hurricane Isaias moves closer.
more: Isaias is expected to make landfall near the Alabama and Florida coasts Friday evening.
local.title: Kemp issues Georgia state of emergency ahead of Hurricane Isaias

local.h: Court: family can't try US over FBI raid
local.b: An appeals court ruled an Atlanta family cannot take the government to trial over a mistaken 2017 FBI raid, but can seek to hold the agent who led the SWAT team liable.
local.title: Appeals court says Atlanta family cannot take the government to trial for a mistaken FBI raid

local.h: UPS to hire 100,000 seasonal workers
local.b: UPS is hiring more than 100,000 seasonal workers nationwide for the holidays, fewer than in past years as it uses more AI.
local.title: UPS will lean on AI and seasonal workers during the holidays

local.h: Bears legend Mike Ditka dies at 86
local.b: Mike Ditka, who played on the Bears' 1963 title team and coached them to their only Super Bowl win, died Friday morning surrounded by family.
local.title: Mike Ditka, who coached the Bears to their only Super Bowl championship, has died

local.h: College covers Flock cameras after refusal
local.b: Elgin Community College covered its Flock license-plate cameras with trash bags after the company refused to remove them, to protect immigrant students.
more: Records show federal immigration authorities accessed Flock data at other Illinois colleges.

local.h: Protesters urge DePaul to reopen art museum
local.b: More than 130 students, faculty and neighbors held a silent demonstration urging DePaul University to reopen its art museum, closed since June 30.
local.title: Students, faculty and neighbors press DePaul University to reopen its art museum

local.h: Block 37 mall sold for $30 million
local.b: Edwards Realty Co. bought the Loop's Block 37 for $30 million and plans to rebrand the mall with a mix of retail and entertainment.

local.h: Villegas González family seeks damages
local.b: The family of Silverio Villegas González, shot dead by an ICE agent during Operation Midway Blitz, filed a complaint seeking compensation from the federal government.
more: The claim under the Federal Tort Claims Act is the first step toward a lawsuit.

local.h: Obama Center workers move to unionize
local.b: More than 250 Obama Foundation and Presidential Center workers are organizing a union with AFSCME Council 31.
more: They cite increasing workloads and benefit rollbacks.

local.h: Chicago Marathon expects record field
local.b: Organizers expect the largest field ever for the 48th Chicago Marathon this weekend.

local.h: Mary Todd Lincoln's cape goes on view
local.b: The bloodstained cape Mary Todd Lincoln wore the night of Lincoln's assassination is part of a new Chicago History Museum exhibit on presidential artifacts.

local.title: Manhattan DA argues judge shouldn't dismiss state charges against Luigi Mangione

local.h: Judge: ICE lied after mistaken Bronx arrests
local.b: A federal judge ruled ICE agents mistakenly arrested two men in the Bronx and then lied in sworn testimony to cover it up.
local.title: ICE mistakenly arrested 2 men in the Bronx, then mounted cover-up, US judge rules

local.h: Council wants paper tests back
local.b: City Council members are calling on education officials to let students return to paper tests as the state mandates screens.
local.title: Pencils down: NYC lawmakers want to switch back to paper tests as state mandates screens

local.h: Five arrested at ICE shooting protest
local.b: Police said five people were taken into custody as protests swelled Thursday night after ICE officers shot a man in northern Manhattan.
more: All were charged with obstructing governmental administration.
local.title: Several arrested in wake of ICE protest where Manhattan man was shot in the neck

local.h: Bronx homeowners seek foreclosure help
local.b: Gothamist reports on Bronx homeowners facing foreclosure and looking for assistance.
local.title: Bronx homeowners facing foreclosure are in the market for assistance

local.h: Cornell students warned of fraternity abuse
local.b: Cornell's student government says it warned administrators about sexual assault and drugging in fraternities two years before the Jane Doe gang rape report.
local.title: Cornell students warned of fraternity 'rape culture' years before Jane Doe case

local.h: Person shot in encounter with federal agents
local.b: A person was shot during an encounter involving federal law enforcement agents in Marble Hill on Thursday afternoon, the NYPD said.
local.title: ICE agent fires 7 rounds, shoots man in neck in NYC's Marble Hill, NYPD says

local.h: Bronx exempt from Medicaid work rule
local.b: Because of high unemployment, Bronx residents will be exempt from Medicaid work requirements when new federal rules take effect in January, the state health department said.
local.title: Bronx residents will be exempt from new Medicaid work rule, state officials say

local.h: MTA chief says Byford went "full MAGA"
local.b: MTA Chair Janno Lieber accused Andy Byford, who leads Amtrak's Penn Station rebuild, of going "full MAGA."
more: President Trump took control of the project from the MTA last year.
local.title: MTA chair accuses Andy Byford, who's leading Penn Station rebuild, of going 'full MAGA'

local.h: Jersey City shakes up staff amid $255M gap
local.b: Jersey City Mayor James Solomon announced the resignations of the city's finance director and deputy mayor for housing amid a $255 million budget gap.
local.title: Jersey City mayor shakes up staff amid $255M budget gap

local.h: Man charged in fatal Queens park stabbing
local.b: Police arrested 53-year-old Abdullah Spencerel on murder charges in a fatal stabbing in Major Mark Park in Queens.
more: A witness pointed officers to him three blocks away; police are still working to identify the victim.
local.title: Bronx man arrested for allegedly stabbing Queens man to death in a public park

local.h: Data centers stir NY governor race
local.b: Gothamist's Jimmy Vielkind writes that the New York governor race pits an old immigration playbook against new outrage over data centers.
local.title: NY gov race pits old immigration playbook against new outrage over data centers

local.h: Survey: NYC parents split on childcare needs
local.b: A New America survey of NYC families with young children found working parents need more weekend childcare, and most want to be the main caregiver in a child's first year.
more: Parents in higher-income areas near Manhattan more often prefer formal preschool for 2-year-olds than parents in the Bronx and parts of Queens.
local.title: NYC parents want affordable childcare. But they don't all want the same thing.

local.h: Arrest in deadly Bronx balcony push
local.b: Police arrested the man they say pushed a 23-year-old mother and their 8-month-old daughter from a Bronx balcony, killing the woman; he faces a murder charge.
local.title: Man who pushed his baby and her mother from a Bronx balcony arrested for murder, NYPD says

local.h: Teen, 15, shot dead in Harlem
local.b: A 15-year-old was shot and killed and a man was wounded at NYCHA's Martin Luther King Jr. Towers in Harlem; police are questioning a teen.
local.title: Harlem community of murdered 15-year-old mourns as NYPD questions teen tied to incident

local.h: Audit questions Newark school spending
local.b: An audit questioning how millions were spent in Newark's public schools led to a referral to state prosecutors, Gothamist reports.
local.title: Audit questions how millions were spent in Newark schools. GOP says it's no surprise.

local.title: France students plan more protests as UN voices ‘concern’ over violence

local.h: Philippe vows to halve legal migration
local.b: Centrist presidential candidate Edouard Philippe said he wants to halve legal migration, laying out his 2027 programme in a TV interview.

local.h: France sends 3,000 substitute teachers
local.b: Education Minister Edouard Geffray said 3,000 substitute teachers will join struggling high schools within hours, after nationwide student protests.

local.h: Lescure: Brexit impact "irrevocable"
local.b: Finance Minister Roland Lescure said he would welcome the UK back in the EU but warned Brexit had irrevocable consequences.
more: He said a return would mean taking "the whole thing," not special terms.

local.h: TotalEnergies strike shuts some fuel stations
local.b: TotalEnergies workers are on strike Thursday, blocking shipments from refineries near Le Havre, at Donges and at La Mède, and closing some petrol stations.

local.h: Le Pen proposes tax on hiring non-EU workers
local.b: Marine Le Pen's counter-budget includes an extra €1,000 a year per worker for companies that employ non-EU nationals.

goodnews.h: Viral vegetarian wolf becomes a toy
goodnews.b: Intermarché will sell 700,000 plush versions of the vegetarian wolf from its viral Christmas advert at the end of November.

local.h: Gluesenkamp Perez, Braun hold first debate
local.b: Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez and state Sen. John Braun split over voter ID and immigration enforcement in their first debate for Washington's 3rd District.
local.title: Gluesenkamp Perez and Braun meet in first debate for Southwest Washington’s battleground House district

local.h: 11,000 WA immigrants lose Medicaid
local.b: About 11,000 refugees, asylum seekers and other lawfully present immigrants in Washington lost Medicaid coverage this month, including 4,000 in King County.
more: Councilmember Teresa Mosqueda called the federal cuts a betrayal.

local.h: WA voters to weigh millionaires tax
local.b: A yes vote on Initiative 645 this November would repeal Washington's new 9.9% tax on household income over $1 million.
more: The tax is also being challenged in court.

local.h: Engine-room sick-out halted WA ferries
local.b: Twenty-three Washington State Ferries engine-room workers called out sick this week over labor concerns, leaving only six of 18 boats running on Monday.
